bullets.title: META: $95B equity raise ($35B now + $60B ATM) with NVDA/AMD/AVGO as $5B cornerstone buyers
bullets.body: Meta launched a $22.5B Class A common + $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred offering (priced Oct 26), plus a separate $60B ATM program via Class C shares slated for Q1 2027. NVDA, AMD, and AVGO each indicated interest in purchasing up to aggregate $5B of Class A. Meta expects $135-145B capex in 2026, funding via OCF, IG debt, strategic partnerships, and this equity. Shares traded up ~1-2% pre-market on dilution overhang being resolved.

bullets.title: VZ Q3 beat: 406K postpaid phone adds, FCF $7.8B, guides raise across the board
bullets.body: VZ reported adj. EPS $1.31 vs. $1.27 est., EBITDA $13.80B vs. $13.71B, and FCF $7.80B vs. ~$6.2B est. Postpaid phone adds of 406K blew past 174-215K consensus on +10% gross add growth. 2026 guidance lifted: postpaid adds to 1.1-1.2M (from 750K-1M), EPS to $5.04-5.06, FCF growth to ~12% (from 9-10%). Offsets: ARPA -1.9% y/y to $168.08 (missed $170.34 est.), FWA adds 159K missed ~200K est. VZ also signed $2B+ AWS deal for distributed AI compute. Citi and KeyBanc (Sector Weight) both neutral; UBS maintains Neutral.

bullets.title: TSLA: Barclays upgrades to Overweight from Equal Weight
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded Tesla to Overweight, sending shares +2.4% pre-market Monday. No detailed PT disclosed in forwarded notes but the upgrade follows Tesla's Q3 automotive gross margins of 18.1% ex-credits, above 16.7% consensus. SpaceX-Tesla AI/autonomous merger narrative also cited as a catalyst.

bullets.title: Neocloud selloff: Musk warns 200+ face 'guppy-level death'; CRWV/IREN -2%+ pre-mkt
bullets.body: Elon Musk posted that debt markets have 'almost entirely shut off' access for companies whose only revenue is AI datacenter rental, predicting widespread neocloud consolidation. CRWV fell -2.4% and IREN -1.9-2.2% Monday pre-market. SpaceX closed its own $40B debt deal (callable bonds) due to investment-grade status and Starlink/launch revenue diversification. GS Prime noted ~$20B of net TMT selling over two weeks, approaching July unwind levels.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye remains short; Dec Q guidance at risk on iPhone 18 demand & memory cost headwinds
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains a short on AAPL at ~38x FY27 P/E, arguing the stock is propped by AI-hedge/defensive buying rather than fundamentals. iPhone 18 Pro lead times have normalized to 7-21 days (in line with prior year), but Duo supply remains constrained at ~94 days. Key bear points: China non-premium share loss, memory cost headwinds persisting into 2027, and expected Dec-Q guidance disappointment. Jefferies separately notes Dec Q may miss on weak iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max demand and memory GM pressure of 5-6ppt.

bullets.title: AMD: UBS sees FQ4 guide as high as $17B (Street $16.2B); server CPU revenue potentially 2x in C2027
bullets.body: UBS previews AMD earnings flagging FQ3 revenue at $13.1-13.3B (high end of guide) and potential FQ4 guide of $17B vs. Street $16.2B, driven by server CPU revenue growing ~26% Q/Q in FQ4. UBS models AMD server CPU revenue doubling from ~$17B in C2026 to ~$34B in C2027. TSMC allocated strong N3 capacity priority for AMD in 1H27.

bullets.title: MU: UBS names best play on $210B server CPU TAM constrained by DRAM supply
bullets.body: UBS raised its C2030 server CPU TAM estimate to $210B (from $175B), but argues memory supply is the binding constraint—unconstrained demand could exceed $500B. AI CPUs require ~1.5TB DRAM today vs. 0.5TB for traditional CPUs. MU preferred over AMD/INTC because it monetizes the memory bottleneck directly. Separately, JPM noted MU confirmed HBM4 in high-volume manufacturing with HBM4E samples shipping.

bullets.title: MSFT: Oppenheimer raises PT to $625 on Azure acceleration; low implied vol (4% vs 8Q avg 7%)
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raised MSFT PT to $625 from $570, with checks supporting sustained Azure and M365 acceleration—capacity, not demand, is the constraint. Azure modeled at 46% CC vs. ~47% buy-side expectations; FY27 capex debate remains key risk. Jefferies flags MSFT implied move of only 4% vs. 8-quarter avg of 7%, suggesting positioning is very long and vol may be underpriced. Wolfe also sees MSFT as a strong earnings setup.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Mixed bias into earnings; Cloud upside vs. Search deceleration; Hedgeye bearish
bullets.body: Jefferies notes GOOGL has a negative bias but is less shorted than in mid-September, with push-pull between cloud strength and search deceleration. Wolfe likes GOOGL heading into print. Hedgeye rates GOOGL bearish (buy $315, sell $339). Opco notes GOOGL/AMZN both reporting this week with AI monetization as the central focus.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS sold out through 2027; Opco sees 3% EPS upside on 43% incremental margins
bullets.body: CEO Jassy confirmed AWS 2026 capacity is sold out, most large 2027 capacity blocks are booked, and meaningful 2028 capacity is already committed. Oppenheimer models AWS revenue upside to $13.2B+ with 43% incremental margins (Street models 39% for 2027). AMZN also signed a $2B+ deal with VZ for distributed AI compute. Reports Thursday after close vs. consensus EPS $1.97/revenue $202.2B.

bullets.title: NOW: Up 73% since last earnings; long bias into print; Wolfe and Opco both bullish
bullets.body: ServiceNow has rallied 73% since the day after last quarter's print and doubled off its lows. Wolfe sees strong commercial and federal business cRPO. Opco raised PT to not specified but is constructive. Jefferies notes NOW is the highest-conviction upside print setup of the week. Reports Wednesday after close vs. consensus EPS $1.02/revenue $4.09B.

bullets.title: INTC: Jefferies/KeyBanc expect beat & raise; server CPU demand outpacing supply
bullets.body: Consensus expects INTC to beat and raise with Dec Q guidance of $17.5-18B vs. Street $16.52B. Server CPU demand is outpacing supply from agentic AI and inference workloads. Evercore notes CPU ASPs rising 15-20% Q/Q as INTC and AMD shift mix to higher core count CPUs in tight supply. INTC Diamond Rapids (1Q27) is closing the performance gap vs. AMD Venice. Reports Thursday after close.

bullets.title: ALAB: UBS flags 3Q/4Q upside; 4Q revenue expected +20% Q/Q; PT cut to $300 from $425
bullets.body: UBS expects Astera Labs to post upside to consensus in both 3Q and 4Q, with Trainium 3 units up ~15% Q/Q driving 4Q revenue growth of ~20% Q/Q. ALAB's Orion platform addresses neocloud/smaller-scale customers and could compete with MRVL. PT was cut from $425 to $300 on sector de-rating but fundamental outlook remains constructive.

bullets.title: STX: Max bullish buyside sentiment (+5); JPM sees HAMR transition as structural advantage vs. WDC
bullets.body: JPM survey shows STX at max bullish buyside sentiment (+5) heading into Tuesday's print (consensus EPS $7.45). JPM favors STX over WDC on HAMR technology lead despite trimming target multiples to mid-teens. UBS also sees STX beating Sept and Dec quarters on HAMR ramp and higher ASPs, though flags HDD downcycle risk in late 2028. CLS buyside sentiment is +3.

bullets.title: CART: Exploring sale; talks with DASH and UBER; Wolfe sees $16-17B takeout value
bullets.body: Instacart is reportedly in preliminary sale discussions with DoorDash and Uber (latter not ongoing per reports). Wolfe estimates takeout value at $16-17B (30-40% premium), calling CART a likely acquisition target. Stock is up +25% YTD and +30% over the past 3+ weeks. Q3 GTV expected +14.75% Y/Y with Q4 guide of +10-13%.

bullets.title: NFLX: Declining engagement and qualified play days; Wolfe downgrades on English content stall
bullets.body: Wolfe downgraded Netflix citing stalled English TV content engine—top 10 English TV viewing hours down -19% y/y since Stranger Things finale. Netflix's TV share fell for a third consecutive month to lowest since May 2025. Netflix also lowered FY26 ad revenue outlook to $2.7B from ~$3B. YouTube TV reached record 15.8% viewing share in August. Hedgeye rates NFLX bearish (buy $62, sell $69).

bullets.title: DKNG: NY sportsbook handle +5% YoY, GGR +79% on hold rate expansion; UBS Buy $48
bullets.body: For the week ending Oct 18, DKNG's NY OSB handle grew +5% YoY (accelerating from +4% prior week) while GGR surged +79% YoY on hold rate of 10.0% (+410bps YoY). October MTD handle +3% YoY with MTD GGR +24% YoY. Citi notes 3Q industry handle up ~9% with GGR up ~3%; DKNG 3Q handle up ~14% QTD. UBS rates Buy at $48 PT on 17x 2028E EBITDA.

bullets.title: FSLR: ROTH bullish at 5x 2027E EBITDA; expects bookings well ahead of typical 1-2GW/quarter range
bullets.body: ROTH views First Solar as attractively valued at ~5x 2027E EBITDA with an integrated cost structure advantage (mid-20s c/W vs. peers at ~40c/W). Expects FSLR to deliver bookings well above the 1-2GW quarterly norm with pricing ~2c/W higher than Q2. ITC/45X extension carries ~80% probability under a Democratic House. Reports Thursday after close vs. consensus EPS $4.67.

bullets.title: SHOP: AI-driven orders up 15x; META Muse partnership; 112x P/E seen as stretched vs. ~$100 fair value
bullets.body: Shopify revenue grew 30% to $11.5B in 2025 with AI-driven orders up ~15-fold since early 2025. Merchant retention among larger customers is 92-97%. SHOP partnered with META on Muse for agentic checkout. However, analysts peg fair value near $100 vs. ~$160 current price (112x operating earnings). JPM Sketch notes Q3 GMV expected +33-34% Y/Y with alt data supporting the trend.

bullets.title: SPOT: Phillip Securities downgrades to Accumulate from Buy; PT $650 (11% upside)
bullets.body: Phillip Securities downgraded Spotify to Accumulate from Buy, maintaining a $650 PT implying ~11% upside from $584. The stock fell -1.2% pre-market Monday. Jefferies separately notes SPOT showed follow-through on a better Q4 gross margin guide last week.
